definitions.explanation: passages or sections copied out from a larger text, selecting only the important or relevant parts

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}から{大事|だいじ}な{部分|ぶぶん}を{抜|ぬ}き{書|が}きした。
examples.english: I copied out the important parts from the book.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{議事録|ぎじろく}から{要点|ようてん}を{抜|ぬ}き{書|が}きにまとめた。
examples.english: I compiled an extract of key points from the meeting minutes.

examples.japanese: {論文|ろんぶん}の{抜|ぬ}き{書|が}きをノートに{残|のこ}しておくと{復習|ふくしゅう}に{役立|やくだ}つ。
examples.english: Keeping excerpts from papers in a notebook is useful for review.

notes:
Refers to the act of selecting and copying out important passages from a text, or the resulting collection of excerpts. A useful study and research technique.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抜|ぬ}き{書|が}きする: to make an extract, to copy out selected parts
- {抜|ぬ}き{書|が}きノート: notebook of excerpts
- {要点|ようてん}の{抜|ぬ}き{書|が}き: extract of key points

ETYMOLOGY:
Composed of {抜|ぬ}き (pulling out, selecting) and {書|が}き (writing). Literally, writing by pulling out selected parts.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引用|いんよう}: quotation, citation — a formal attribution of someone else's words, with the source specified
- {抜粋|ばっすい}: excerpt, extract — more formal, often used for officially selected portions of documents
- {要約|ようやく}: summary — condenses the content into fewer words rather than copying verbatim
